title: Grateful Dead Live at University of Iowa on 1982-08-10
lineage: SBD -> Cm -> Dat -> Samplitude 2496 v6.0 -> CD -> EAC -> SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of an electrifying 1982 Iowa City show, featuring a smoking Eyes solo, blazing Bertha and a killer second‑set sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as crystal‑clear with superb channel separation, despite a brief early‑set PA hiccup. Musically the concert is described as one of the band’s best of the ’80s – high energy throughout, standout performances of Eyes of the World, Bertha, China Cat > Rider and an unforgettable Iko Iko/​Stella Blue combo. Reviewers repeatedly call it a must‑have for any Dead collection.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews, almost all 5‑star, uniformly praising both the performance and the technical quality; only minor occasional comments about early‑set PA issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, crisp mix with excellent channel separation; a few reviewers note a high‑end distortion in the first six songs that settles after the band’s break, but overall the sound is balanced and vivid.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Fans rave about the tight flow, especially the fire‑breathing second set that moves from a powerful Bertha into an unstoppable China Cat > Rider and culminates with epic Eyes and Iko Iko jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His solos (especially on Eyes of the World and Feel Like a Stranger) are described as perfect, breakneck yet lyrical, with a tone that “just drops jaws.”
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work is solid; some note the mix places Phil low but his playing still provides a strong foundation and occasional “Phil bombs” vibe.
band_member_comments.Bob: Keyboardist Brent’s vocals on Iko Iko receive high praise (“prophetic,” “beautiful”), though one reviewer jokingly calls his voice child‑like. Keyboard work is generally lauded.
band_member_comments.Keys: Same as Bob – Brent’s keyboard and vocal contributions are highlighted positively throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s snare kick is singled out for propelling Jerry’s solo; drums are noted for tight channel separation, energetic drive and overall excellent performance.
